requirements.requirement: Run inventory-api as a managed (systemd) service on node1, serving HTTP
requirements.summary: systemd unit inventory-api.service created, enabled, and started (systemctl is-active=active, is-enabled=enabled). HTTP endpoints /health and /inventory returned valid JSON both immediately after deployment and after the later reboot, confirming durable managed-service behavior.

requirements.requirement: Service keeps serving when a memory-hungry process drives the system out of memory, with the hog (not inventory-api) being the process the kernel stops
requirements.summary: A default-priority (oom_score_adj=0) memory hog was launched and grew to ~1.7GB RSS, triggering a genuine kernel OOM event (global_oom, constraint=CONSTRAINT_NONE) captured in dmesg: 'Out of memory: Killed process 1344 (python3) ... oom_score_adj:0'. inventory-api, configured with OOMScoreAdjust=-1000 (verified live via /proc/PID/oom_score_adj == -1000), remained active throughout with the same MainPID (1313) and continued answering /health both during and after the event.

overall_summary: Both material outcomes of the task are satisfied with direct, coherent evidence: inventory-api is deployed as an enabled systemd service and, during a real kernel OOM event, the default-priority memory hog was killed by the kernel while the protected (OOMScoreAdjust=-1000) inventory-api process continued running and serving requests uninterrupted. The independently-required node-restart evidence protocol was also executed correctly and fully, with pre/post boot-identity change and post-restart service/data recovery cross-checked against the fixed lifecycle snapshots. No unnecessary or unreverted mutations were found in the command trace.
limitations: The memory-hog process ran within the agent's own vsock-agent.service cgroup (per dmesg task_memcg field) rather than a fully isolated context, though the OOM event itself was reported as a global, unconstrained OOM (constraint=CONSTRAINT_NONE), so this does not undermine the validity of the demonstration.

One command (cmd-69e9b7e9d3e14b9c) ended with 'exec stream closed before command completion' (return_code -1) while polling for the OOM event; the actual kill and recovery were independently confirmed by the subsequent command (cmd-a1ff5f8b158443c8), so this truncation does not affect the outcome assessment.

operational_hygiene.summary: All state-changing commands map cleanly to task or protocol purposes: app/unit/user creation for the service (cmd-7470607548a44dd8), the memory hog launch as a necessary in-task demonstration of the OOM-protection requirement (cmd-69e9b7e9d3e14b9c), cleanup of hog artifacts and dmesg marker files immediately afterward (cmd-5817fbef09fd4c00), and the scheduled reboot for the mandatory restart protocol (cmd-29d7945175a64906). No unnecessary or unreverted mutations were found; failed-services and package-health checks show no drift between after-prepare and after-executor snapshots aside from expected boot-identity/socket/tmp changes from the deliberate reboot. The mandatory node-restart protocol was executed cleanly on node1: pre-restart baseline (cmd-5817fbef09fd4c00, boot_id f54d7366...) differs from post-restart boot identity (cmd-6028dfcfc2704691, boot_id 4bd3118c...), corroborated independently by the fixed after_executor snapshot, with full service/data recovery confirmed (cmd-58871afb0ca944e3).
